neighbours.label: a word-start fragment (' Se', '-st', ' sc', ' Stre') that begins a severity or injury word in medical text (Se|vere, blood-st|reaked, sc|arring, Stre|ptococcus); the same words as single tokens or the same fragments in non-medical words stay quiet
fire: The patient arrived with blood-streaked vomit after the fall.
Severe dehydration can follow days of diarrhea in infants.
Severe burns on the hands need specialist wound care.
His saliva was blood-stained and he complained of chest pain.
Streptococcal pharyngitis is treated with penicillin.
Severe allergic reactions can close the airway within minutes.
The nurse noted blood-streaked urine on the second day.
Severe anemia left her pale and short of breath.
quiet: The patient arrived with mild bruising after the fall.
Untreated, severe dehydration can follow days of diarrhea.
Burns on the hands can be severe and need wound care.
His saliva was clear and he complained of chest pain.
Stochastic models of pharyngitis outbreaks guide planning.
In rare cases, severe allergic reactions close the airway.
The nurse noted clear urine on the second day.
Severn Valley clinics treat anemia in pale, tired patients.

notes: The + pole fires on the same s-fragments in neutral words (St|ochastic, _st|ations, ст|ерео), so the two poles split one fragment by medical vs neutral continuation. Probing: '-st' (streaked) 0.92, ' Se' (Severe) 0.59, ' sc' (scarring) 0.16; 'stations' 0.003. Near misses: lowercase ' severe' is a single token, or the fragment starts a non-medical word.
